name: Japanese lessons
about: The path through the first Japanese words, a few at a time, each in everyday sentences written for its lesson, every word with kanji with its kana until you know it well.

words.帰る: to go home, to go back
words.寝る: to sleep, to go to bed
words.起きる: to wake up, to get up
words.止まる: to stop, to come to a stop
words.な: linking form after a な adjective
words.頼む: to ask, to request, to entrust
words.休む: to rest, to take a break
words.連絡する: to contact, to get in touch
words.使い方: how to use, way of using
words.困る: to have trouble, to be at a loss
words.終わる: to finish, to come to an end
words.くれる: to give to me or my group
words.見える: to be visible, to be able to see
words.辞める: to quit, to leave a job
words.覚える: to remember, to learn by heart
words.見つかる: to be found, to turn up
words.なる: to become; to do, to be acceptable
words.遊ぶ: to play, to spend time together
words.相談する: to consult, to discuss a concern
words.気をつける: to be careful, to pay attention
words.失敗する: to fail, to make a mistake
words.通る: to pass through, to go along
words.守る: to follow a rule; to protect
words.十日: tenth day of the month; ten days
words.落ち込む: to feel down, to become discouraged

sumimasen.about: To get someone's attention, or to say sorry.

onegaishimasu.about: Asking for something: コーヒーをお願いします (coffee, please).

arigatou.text: ありがとうございます

kekkou.about: Turning something down politely: いいえ、けっこうです。

konnichiwa.about: Said in the daytime; は in it is said wa.

hajimemashite.about: A greeting when meeting someone for the first time.

yoroshiku.text: よろしくお願いします
yoroshiku.about: A conventional closing to an introduction; it asks for a good relationship.

omachi.about: A courteous request used by staff speaking to a guest: お + 待ち + ください.

items.text: 手すりがあれば、使ってください。

wrong: 川で見つけたの犬の写真を見てください。

items.text: その犬は午後二時に救助されました。
items.means: That dog was rescued at two in the afternoon.
words: きゅうじょされました
wrong: その犬は午後二時に救助されましたです。

items.text: 深い川には入らないでください。
items.means: Please don't go into a deep river.
wrong: 深いな川には入らないでください。

items.text: 動物を救助することは難しいです。
items.means: Rescuing animals is difficult.
wrong: 動物を救助するなことは難しいです。

items.text: 父も昔、犬を救助しました。
items.means: My father also rescued a dog a long time ago.
wrong: 父を昔、犬を救助しました。

items.text: 最初に旅行の写真を見せてください。
items.means: First, please show me the photos from your trip.
wrong: 最初に旅行の写真を見せますください。

items.text: 今日の結果を報告します。
items.means: I'll report today’s results.
wrong: 今日の結果が報告します。

items.text: とてもいい経験でした。
items.means: It was a very good experience.
wrong: とてもいいな経験でした。

items.text: 最初は少し不安でした。
items.means: I was a little worried at first.
wrong: 最初は少し不安だです。

items.text: 最初に会った人について話してください。
items.means: Please tell me about the first person you met.
wrong: 最初に会ったの人について話してください。

items.text: その経験は今も心に残っています。
items.means: That experience is still with me.
wrong: その経験は今も心に残りています。

items.text: 会議で仕事の結果を報告してください。
items.means: Please report the results of your work at the meeting.
wrong: 会議で仕事の結果を報告しでください。

items.text: 先生がいらっしゃいます。経験を話してください。
items.means: The teacher is here. Please share your experience.
wrong: 先生がいらっしゃいます。経験を話しますください。

items.text: 最後にみんなに結果を報告します。
items.means: Finally, I'll tell everyone the results.
wrong: 最後にみんなを結果を報告します。

words.means: コーヒー = coffee
お茶 = tea (green tea)
お水 = water
牛乳 = milk
私 = I, me
飲みます = drink
は = what the sentence is about (said wa)
を = what's drunk (said o)
と = and

concept.line: を (said o) marks what's drunk, and the verb comes last: 私はコーヒーを飲みます (I coffee drink).

words.means: はい = yes
いいえ = no
一つ = one (thing): コーヒーを一つ
元気 = well, fine (in good health)
です = is, am, are
か = makes it a question
とても = very
食べます = eat
も = too

concept.line: か at the end makes a question, and nothing else moves: 元気です (I'm well) → 元気ですか (are you well?, how are you?).

words.means: 本 = book
新聞 = newspaper
読みます = read; 読んでいます = am reading
何 = what (said なに before を)
飲んでいます = am drinking

concept.line: -ています says it's going on now: 読みます (I read) → 読んでいます (I'm reading); 飲みます → 飲んでいます.

lessons.title: Find the phone on the table

words.means: スマホ = phone (a smartphone)
テーブル = table
かばん = bag
どこ = where
の = of: テーブルの上 (the table's top: on the table)
上 = top: テーブルの上 = on the table
中 = inside: かばんの中 = in the bag

concept.line: は (said wa) marks what you're talking about, and です what it is or where: スマホはテーブルの上です (as for the phone, the table's top it is).

words.means: 車 = car
ここ = here
あそこ = over there

concept.line: です says what something is, or where: 車はここです (as for the car, here it is). It doesn't change for I, you or it.

words.means: 鍵 = key
まだ = still
準備 = getting ready: 準備はいいですか (are you ready?)
いい = good, fine
もう = now, already

concept.line: いい (good) takes です, as every い adjective does: 準備はいいですか (is the getting-ready good?: are you ready?), はい、いいです.

words.means: 友達 = friend

concept.line: の joins two nouns, the owner first: 私の鍵 (my key), 友達のスマホ (my friend's phone); after an owner alone it means the one of: 私のです (it's mine).

words.means: 母 = my mom (said of your own mother)

lessons.title: On the table, in the bag

words.means: が = what's there (said ga)
あります = is there (a thing)
います = is there (a person or animal)
に = in, on, at (where something is)

concept.line: に marks where something is; あります says a thing is there, います a person: テーブルの上にお茶があります (on the table there's tea); 母は車の中にいます.

words.means: 家 = house, home
帰ります = go home
で = at (where you do something)
ください = please (after a verb's て form: 帰ってください)
飲んで = drink (with ください: please drink)
読んで = read (with ください: please read)

concept.line: で marks where you do something, に where you go: 家でお茶を飲みます (at home I drink tea); 家に帰ります (I go home).

words.means: 飲みません = don't drink
帰りません = don't go home
読みません = don't read

concept.line: -ません in place of -ます makes a verb not: 飲みます (drink) → 飲みません (don't drink). There's no do: the verb's ending says it.

words.means: 飲みたい = want to drink; 飲みましょう = let's drink
食べたい = want to eat; 食べましょう = let's eat
一緒 = together (一緒に)

concept.line: A verb's -ます part with たいです says what you want to do: 飲みます → 飲みたいです (I want to drink); with ましょう, let's: 飲みましょう.
-ます is the same for I, you, he and she: 私は飲みます, 母は飲みます; who it is comes from は, or isn't said at all.

words.means: できます = can do
手伝えます = can help; 手伝えません = can't help
読めます = can read

concept.line: できます says can do: 何ができますか (what can I do?); a verb's can form: 手伝えます (can help), 読めます (can read); what you can takes が.

words.means: 帰りましょう = let's go home

concept.line: と after a person means with: 母と帰ります (I go home with Mom); 一緒に (together) often goes with it: 私と一緒に (together with me).

words.means: これ = this (one)
この = this (before a noun): この鍵

concept.line: これ (this one) stands alone: これは私の鍵です; before a noun it's この: この鍵 (this key). It doesn't change for the noun.

lessons.title: I still have work to do

words.means: 仕事 = work, a job
ありません = there isn't, don't have

concept.line: What you have takes が, with あります: 仕事があります (work is there: I have work); with ありません, you don't: 仕事がありません.

words.means: だれ = who: だれの (whose)
それ = that (one)
その = that (before a noun): その鍵
だれか = someone; anyone in a question
ドア = door
開けます = open; 開けて = open, before ください; 開けましょう = let's open
来ます = come

concept.line: A verb’s て form with ください asks someone to do it: ドアを開けてください (please open the door). だれか means someone, or anyone in a question.

words.means: 今 = now
時間 = time
手伝いましょう = let's help; with か, shall I help?
どう = how; どうですか also offers something

concept.line: -ましょうか offers to do something: 手伝いましょうか (shall I help?). The person is left out when it is clear.

words.means: 今日 = today
探しています = am looking for; 探しましょう = let's look for
なくしました = lost; なくしません = won't lose
姉 = my older sister

concept.line: -ました makes a polite verb past: なくしました (I lost it). 探しています says the search is happening now; 姉 means your own older sister when you speak about her.

words.means: 二 = two
時 = o'clock, after the hour
予約 = appointment, reservation
医者 = doctor

concept.line: A clock time takes に when it says when something happens: 二時に予約があります (I have an appointment at two). 二時です says it is at two.

words.means: お金 = money
払います = pay
か = or, between alternatives
見ます = look, see; 見て = look, before ください; 見ました = saw
そこ = there, near you
何か = something; anything in a question
下 = underneath: テーブルの下 means under the table

concept.line: そこ means there, near the listener. With に it says where something is: そこに何かあります (there is something there).

words.means: だれ = who
男 = male: 男の人 means a man
人 = person
知っています = know, be acquainted with

concept.line: 知っています means know: the state of knowing, not an action happening now. Ask who with だれ: だれが来ますか (who is coming?).

words.means: いつ = when
どうして = why

concept.line: A question word stays where its answer would: 何を探していますか (what are you looking for?), 予約はいつですか (when is the appointment?). か at the end asks the question; だれか and 何か mean someone and something.

words.means: 住んでいます = live, have your home
町 = town
働いています = work, be employed; 働きます = will work

concept.line: 住んでいます says where you live; 働いています says where you work. These are states that hold. A home takes に, and the place you work takes で.

words.means: 作ります = make; 作りましょう = let's make; 作っています = am making
みんな = everyone; みんなで means all together

concept.line: みんなで means all together: みんなでお茶を作りましょう (let’s all make tea). で also marks where an action happens.

words.means: 電話します = phone, call someone
ちょっと = a little; softens a request
手伝って = help, before ください

concept.line: 手伝ってください asks someone to help. ちょっと softens it: ちょっと手伝ってください (please give me a hand).

words.means: 今晩 = tonight
一人 = one person; 一人で means alone
静か = quiet

concept.line: 静か is a な adjective. Here it comes before です, with no な: 家は静かです (the house is quiet). 一人で means alone.

words.means: 質問 = question
聞きます = ask, listen; 聞きたい = want to ask; 聞いて = listen, before ください
について = about, after the topic of a question

concept.line: 聞きます can mean ask or listen. 質問を聞いてください asks someone to listen to the question; 姉に聞きます says who you ask, with に.

words.means: 待ちます = wait; 待っています = am waiting; 待って = wait, before ください
外 = outside
まで = until, after the ending time
三 = three

concept.line: まで marks the endpoint: 三時まで待ちます (I will wait until three). With です, 仕事は三時までです means work lasts until three.

words.means: 聞こえます = can hear; 聞こえました = could hear
分かります = understand; 分かりました = understood, got it

concept.line: Change -ます to -ました for the past: 聞こえます → 聞こえました (could hear), 分かります → 分かりました (understood). Add か to ask whether it happened.

words.means: 一杯 = one cup, one glass
おいしい = delicious
ください = please give me, after the thing requested

concept.line: 一杯 counts one cup or glass: コーヒーを一杯ください (one cup of coffee, please). もう一杯 asks for another.

words.means: いくら = how much
二百 = two hundred
三百 = three hundred
円 = yen, after the amount
買います = buy

concept.line: Ask a price with いくら: この本はいくらですか (how much is this book?). The amount comes before 円: 三百円 (three hundred yen).

words.means: 何時 = what time, said なんじ
始まります = start; 始まりました = started
映画 = film, movie
五 = five

concept.line: 何時 (なんじ) asks the clock time; 何時に asks at what time. It is one question word here, separate from 何 (なに): 映画は何時に始まりますか.

words.means: 分かりません = don't understand
言葉 = word, language
難しい = difficult

concept.line: 分かりません says you do not understand. What you do not understand takes が, or は as the topic: この言葉が分かりません (I do not understand this word).

lessons.title: A busy day at the office

words.means: いつも = always
忙しい = busy
会社 = company, office
行きます = go

concept.line: 会社に行きます says you go to the office, with に. 会社で働いています says you work there, with で. Busy is 忙しいです.

words.means: ベッド = bed
寝ます = go to bed, sleep; 寝ています = am asleep; 寝たい = want to sleep
起きます = get up; 起きません = won't get up

concept.line: 寝ています describes being asleep. 寝ます says you sleep or are going to bed; 寝たいです says you want to sleep. 起きます means get up.

words.means: 少し = a little
だけ = only, just
欲しい = want a thing, with が and です

concept.line: A thing you want takes が before 欲しいです: お水が欲しいです (I want some water). 欲しい describes wanting a thing; 飲みたい describes wanting to drink. 少しだけ means just a little.

words.means: 高い = expensive; 高くない = not expensive
忙しくない = not busy
じゃない = not, after a noun or a な adjective

concept.line: An い adjective changes its final い to くない: 高くないです (not expensive), 忙しくないです (not busy). A な adjective takes じゃないです: 静かじゃないです (not quiet). Money or time you do not have still takes ありません.

words.means: 試しましょう = let's try; 試します = try; 試して = try, before ください
パン = bread

concept.line: 試しましょう suggests trying something: このお茶を試しましょう (let's try this tea). 試してください asks the listener to try it. Both keep polite endings.

words.means: 犬 = dog
公園 = park
散歩します = take a walk; 散歩しています = am taking a walk; 散歩しましょう = let's take a walk

concept.line: 犬と says with the dog, just as 友達と says with a friend. 公園で散歩します says where the walk happens; 公園に行きます says where you go.

words.means: 部屋 = room
いす = chair
置きます = put, place; 置いて = put, before ください

concept.line: に marks where you put something: ここにいすを置きます (I'll put a chair here). The thing you put takes を. 置いてください asks someone to put it there.

words.means: 昨日 = yesterday
話 = story, talk
面白かった = was interesting; 面白い = interesting
でした = was, were

concept.line: An い adjective changes い to かった before です: 面白かったです (was interesting). A な adjective uses でした: 静かでした (was quiet). Do not put でした after an unchanged い adjective.

words.means: 思います = think, with と before it
来る = come, the dictionary form before と思います
帰る = go home, the dictionary form before と思います
始まる = start, the dictionary form before と思います
と = marks the thought before 思います

concept.line: Put the thought before と思います. The verb inside uses its dictionary form: 来ます → 来る, 帰ります → 帰る, 始まります → 始まる. 思います keeps the sentence polite. Time can come before place, but that order is not a fixed rule.

words.means: どの = which, before a noun
見たい = want to watch; 見ましょう = let's watch
長い = long

concept.line: どの asks which before a noun: どの映画 (which film). With が you can ask which one has a quality. An い adjective goes straight before と思います: 長いと思います (I think it is long).

words.means: 見せて = show, before ください; 見せます = show

concept.line: 中を見せてください asks someone to show you inside. 見せて is the て form of 見せます (show); 見て is from 見ます (look). The listener is asked to show you something, not to look at it.

words.means: 遅れました = was late; 遅れます = will be late
から = because, after the reason
電車 = train
止まりました = stopped; 止まります = stop, will stop

concept.line: Put から after the reason: 電車が止まりましたから、遅れました (I was late because the train stopped). Keep ます or です before から in this round. The reason comes first; the result follows.

lessons.title: Spending a day off at home

words.means: 休み = day off, break
九 = nine, said く before 時
起きて = get up and then, before the next action
食べて = eat and then, before the next action
から = from, after the starting time

concept.line: The て form joins actions in order: 起きて、パンを食べます (I get up and eat bread). Only the last verb gives tense and politeness. 二時から三時まで means from two until three; から follows a time here, not a reason.

words.means: 電話 = telephone; 電話番号 means telephone number
番号 = number, such as a telephone number
教えます = tell, teach; 教えて = tell, before ください
電話して = call, before ください

concept.line: 電話番号を教えてください asks someone to tell you their phone number. 教えます is the natural verb for giving someone this information. The number takes を; the person you tell takes に.

words.means: コップ = drinking glass
水 = water, without the polite お prefix
持ってきます = bring; 持ってきて = bring, before ください

concept.line: 持ってきてください asks someone to bring something here. The thing takes を; に can mark who it is for or where it is brought. 水 is the same water as お水, without the polite prefix.

words.means: しました = did; します = do
働きました = worked
忙しかった = was busy

concept.line: -ました asks or tells what happened: 何をしましたか (what did you do?), 働きました (worked). Describing the past uses the adjective's own form: 忙しかったです (was busy).

lessons.title: What did you have for lunch?

words.means: 昼ご飯 = lunch
食べました = ate
飲みました = drank
おいしかった = was delicious

concept.line: 食べました and 飲みました are polite past forms. 昼ご飯に says for lunch: 昼ご飯に何を食べましたか. To say it tasted good, use おいしかったです, the adjective's past form.

words.means: 駅 = station
行きました = went
帰りました = went home, came back

concept.line: 行きました says went; 帰りました says went home or came back. Keep the destination's に in the past, and add か to ask: どこに行きましたか. 駅から says from the station.

words.means: 音楽 = music
聞きました = listened, heard; 聞いています = am listening
説明 = explanation

concept.line: 音楽を聞きます means listen to music; 説明を聞きます means listen to an explanation. Both take を. 聞いています is listening now; 聞きました says you listened or heard it.

words.means: 会います = meet; 会いました = met
乗ります = get on, ride; 乗りました = got on, rode
出ます = leave, go out; 出ました = left, went out

concept.line: Learn a verb with its particle: 友達を待ちます (wait for a friend), 友達に会います (meet a friend), 電車に乗ります (get on a train), 家を出ます (leave home). を after 家 marks the place left, not something acted on. 会います can also take と for a mutual meeting.

words.means: 話したい = want to talk; 話します = talk; 話せます = can talk; 話せません = can't talk

concept.line: 話せます says can talk; 話せません says cannot. 今、話せますか asks the listener if they can talk now, with no word for you. だれかと話したいです says you want someone to talk to.

words.means: 学校 = school
近く = near, the nearby area
前 = front; 学校の前 means in front of the school

concept.line: A place followed by の近く means near it; の前 means in front of it. 学校は駅の近くです says the school is near the station.

words.means: 大きい = big
きれい = beautiful, clean; a な adjective despite its final い

concept.line: 大きい is an い adjective. きれい is a な adjective, despite ending in い. Both take です when describing the house: この家はきれいです.

words.means: 子供 = child, children
二人 = two people
出ましょう = let's go out, let's leave

concept.line: 子供が二人います says there are two children, or that you have two children. 二人で means the two of us or two people together. The noun itself does not need a plural ending.

words.means: 奥さん = your wife, someone else's wife
妻 = my wife, said of your own
お名前 = name, politely; 名前 = name

concept.line: 奥さんのお名前 means your wife's name. 奥さん is used for someone else's wife; 妻 for your own. お名前 is the polite form of 名前, used when asking about someone else.

lessons.title: Taking a book to your brother

words.means: 兄 = my older brother
持っていきます = take something there; 持っていって = take, before ください

concept.line: 兄に本を持っていきます means taking a book to your older brother. に marks who it is for. 持っていく is learned as one expression, taking something away from here; 持ってくる brings it here.

words.means: 質問します = ask a question; 質問して = ask a question, before ください
先生 = teacher

concept.line: 質問してください invites someone to ask questions. The person asked takes に: 先生に質問してください. The topic of a question can still take について.

words.means: 手 = hand
痛い = painful, hurts; 痛くない = doesn't hurt
右 = right; 右の手 means right hand
左 = left; 左の手 means left hand

concept.line: 手が痛いです says your hand hurts. 痛い is an い adjective; 痛くないです says it does not hurt. 右の手 and 左の手 use the familiar noun link の.

lessons.title: Asking someone to put a book here

words.means: 置かないで = don't put, before ください
開けないで = don't open, before ください

concept.line: The negative form plus でください asks someone not to do something: 置く becomes 置かない, so 置かないでください means please don't put it there. 開ける becomes 開けない: 開けないでください. These negative forms are used only inside polite requests here.

words.means: 道 = road, way
通行止め = closed to traffic
止まって = stop, before ください

concept.line: この道は通行止めです says this road is closed to traffic. Add から after the polite reason, then the request: 通行止めですから、ここで止まってください.

words.means: あと = another, more, before a remaining amount
一分 = one minute
急がないで = don't hurry, before ください; 急ぎます = hurry

concept.line: あと一分 asks for one more minute. A duration goes directly before 待ってください, without に. 急がないでください says please don't hurry.

words.means: 運転 = driving
習います = take lessons in, learn from someone; 習っています = am learning
運転します = drive

concept.line: 運転を習っています describes taking driving lessons. 習います uses に for the teacher. 運転します means drive; 運転ができます asks or says whether someone can drive.

words.means: 楽しい = fun, enjoyable; 楽しかった = was fun
笑っています = is smiling, is laughing

concept.line: 楽しい becomes 楽しかった before です for the past. Ask whether school was fun with 学校は楽しかったですか. 笑っています reports visible smiling or laughter.

words.means: 意味 = meaning
どういう = what kind of; どういう意味 asks what something means

concept.line: Learn どういう意味 as the expression for what meaning: この言葉はどういう意味ですか asks what this word means. どういう stays immediately before 意味; it is not a new verb pattern here.

words.means: 新しい = new
使います = use; 使って = use, before ください; 使えます = can use

concept.line: 使います means use; 使えます means can use. このスマホは使えますか asks whether this phone can be used, not for permission. 新しい describes the phone before です in this lesson.
